source: How to Break Software by James Whittaker: the user-interface attacks on inputs, outputs, stored data and computation. Descriptions are ours.

heuristics.name: Force every error message
heuristics.description: Every error message the product can show is a path someone wrote and few tested.
heuristics.apply: Find the product's error messages (from docs, validation hints, the UI) and try to trigger each one.

heuristics.name: Force the defaults
heuristics.description: Leaving fields at their default, or clearing a default, runs code paths users rarely take.
heuristics.apply: Submit forms without touching the defaults, then clear each default and submit again.

heuristics.name: Explore character sets
heuristics.description: Characters outside plain letters and digits trip up storage, search and display.
heuristics.apply: Enter control characters, symbols and characters from other scripts in every text field.

heuristics.name: Overflow input limits
heuristics.description: Inputs longer than the field's limit may be cut silently, rejected, or break the page.
heuristics.apply: Type or paste past each field's maximum length and compare what's saved with what you entered.

heuristics.name: Inputs that interact
heuristics.description: Two fields that depend on each other (start and end date, quantity and stock) can be set to disagree.
heuristics.apply: Set related fields to contradict each other, such as an end date before a start date.

heuristics.name: Repeat the same input
heuristics.description: Doing the same thing many times can build up state until something overflows or duplicates.
heuristics.apply: Repeat one action many times in a row, like adding the same item or applying the same filter.

heuristics.name: Force different outputs
heuristics.description: An input usually has one common result; the rarer results are less tested.
heuristics.apply: For one action, find inputs that give each possible outcome, not just the usual one.

heuristics.name: Force invalid outputs
heuristics.description: Some inputs make the product produce output that shouldn't exist, like a negative total or an impossible date.
heuristics.apply: Look for inputs that would make a shown value impossible, and check the product prevents it.

heuristics.name: Change output size
heuristics.description: Output that grows or shrinks (long names, many results) can break layouts and tables.
heuristics.apply: Make shown content much longer or shorter than usual, and check the page still lays out and updates.

heuristics.name: Force a refresh
heuristics.description: Views that should update after a change may show stale data until reloaded.
heuristics.apply: Change something, then check every other view that shows it updates without a manual reload.

heuristics.name: Overflow stored data
heuristics.description: Stored collections have limits (items in a cart, rows in a list) that may not be enforced.
heuristics.apply: Add more and more items to a collection until something changes, and note how the product reacts.

heuristics.name: Invalid calculations
heuristics.description: Calculations fail on zero, huge values and values that don't fit the formula.
heuristics.apply: Feed calculated fields values that would divide by zero, overflow or make no sense.

heuristics.name: Feature interaction
heuristics.description: Two features that each work may fail when used together or on the same data.
heuristics.apply: Use two features on the same item one after the other, such as a filter and paging, or a discount and a quantity change.
